_amendments.what: eslint.config.mjs sets preserve-caught-error to "warn" (not "off") repo-wide, instead of the original plan (REPORT the new eslint:recommended error and HALT, deferring the fix to a separate slice).
_amendments.why: pnpm lint is canonical verification for every registered slice, including concurrent, unrelated ones (docs/autopilot-INFLIGHT.md showed 2 other lanes active at authorship time). Landing with this rule at its default "error" severity — even behind a HALT-and-defer plan — means the FIRST slice to merge with it unresolved turns `pnpm lint` red for every other lane, not just this one. That cost was not weighed in the original negative_scope, which predates the rule's existence (v10 added it; the manifest was authored against v9's rule set). "warn" (not "off") was chosen specifically because level 4 of the project's decision-priority order rejects debt that depends on someone remembering: "off" is a silent, memory-dependent exception; "warn" reprints the reminder on every lint run while keeping CI green.

focused: test -f .autopilot/state/eslint-10-migration/design-probe-file-list.txt && npx eslint . -f json | node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(0,"utf8"));const files=d.map(function(x){return x.filePath.replace(process.cwd()+"/","");}).sort();for(const f of files)console.log(f)' | diff .autopilot/state/eslint-10-migration/design-probe-file-list.txt -

_verification_note: Stated as PROPERTIES, never literals. Command 1 diffs the post-upgrade linted-file set against a baseline the design probe MUST capture before any edit (Steps step 3 in the slice doc) into .autopilot/state/eslint-10-migration/design-probe-file-list.txt — a changed file set fails the diff regardless of which direction it moved, so a narrower OR wider set both correctly HALT via VERIFICATION_FAILED. Command 2 is the actual proof the security consequence happened (E10-3), not a hope. Command 3 is DELIBERATELY NARROW, not a full semver-range evaluator: it asserts the currently-measured bad literal `>=22` is gone, which mechanically catches the most likely failure mode (forgetting to touch engines.node at all, or replacing it with something that still reads exactly `>=22`). It does NOT prove the new range fully excludes 22.0.0-22.12.x — that requires reading the actual chosen range string, which is the coding agent's and the code-review round's job (E10-5's full property is also a named acceptance criterion for that reason). A `npx --yes semver`-based general range check was tried and rejected 2026-07-31: it is an undeclared external package fetch (blocked by this environment's own execution policy) AND it silently produced a WRONG answer in testing (reported the then-current bad `>=22` range as already satisfying the property) — a fragile, unverifiable check is worse than an honestly-narrower one. Command 4 is a fixed-string (-F) match on a comment-adjacent code block that this slice must not touch, plus a real lint run scoped to scripts/.

security_review.reason: devDependency toolchain upgrade only (eslint + its plugin ecosystem) — no trust boundary, auth, secret, money, external-input or deployment surface is touched. The security benefit (removing the brace-expansion@1 branch, GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg) is a structural side effect of the version bump and is verified mechanically by verification.focused, not something that needs adversarial review.
security_review.void_if: eslint.config.mjs changes end up disabling or weakening any currently-enabled security-relevant rule, or the engines.node/package.json edit is found to affect resolution of any non-dev runtime dependency — if either happens, this judgement is void: add a security round and say why.

_problem: ESLint v9.x reaches END-OF-LIFE on 2026-08-06 and will not be maintained after that; the repo runs eslint ^9.18.0 resolving to 9.39.4. This upgrade is driven by that date, not by a feature need. It also closes a security item for free: eslint 9 pulls minimatch 3.1.5 (directly, plus via @eslint/config-array@0.21.2 and @eslint/eslintrc@3.3.5), which pulls brace-expansion 1.1.16, which is covered by GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (CVSS 7.5, affected <= 5.0.7, patched only in 5.0.8 -- so the v1 branch has NO in-range fix). ESLint v10.0.0 lists `501abd0 feat!: update dependency minimatch to v10 (#20246)` as a breaking change, so v10 removes that branch entirely. This was split out of `deps-security-bump` on 2026-07-29 because a major toolchain upgrade does not belong in a dependency-floor slice.
_why_not_the_other_route: Forcing `brace-expansion@1` to ^5 via an override is NOT an option and must not be attempted: v1 is `module.exports = expandTop` (a function) while v5 CJS is `exports.expand` (an object), and the sole consumer minimatch@3.1.5 calls `require('brace-expansion')(...)` as a function. pnpm resolves it cleanly, nothing fails at install, and lint dies at call time with `expand is not a function`. Measured 2026-07-29.
_design_probe_findings: MEASURED 2026-07-29 on main@f83995f -- the three compat questions the backlog block flagged are now CLOSED, all favourably. Recorded here so the slice does not re-derive them, but `_evidence_rules` still requires re-measuring at execution time. (a) typescript-eslint 8.62.1 -- root package and all three sub-packages (@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin, /parser, /utils) already declare `peerDependencies.eslint: ^8.57.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0`. ESLint 10 is ALREADY supported by the installed version; NO typescript-eslint upgrade is required. This was the single biggest risk because `tseslint.config()` is the frame of the entire eslint.config.mjs. (b) @next/eslint-plugin-next 15.5.20 declares NO peerDependencies at all and its only dependency is fast-glob, so it does not constrain the eslint version. Absence of a peer range is not proof of compatibility, so the plugin source was grepped for every API v10 removes -- context.getCwd(), getFilename(), getPhysicalFilename(), getSourceCode(), context.parserOptions, context.parserPath, SourceCode#getTokenOrCommentBefore/After, isSpaceBetweenTokens, getJSDocComment -- ZERO hits on all ten. (c) Node: ESLint 10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Local is v22.22.3 (satisfies); CI declares `node-version: 22` which resolves to the newest 22.x (satisfies). BUT package.json declares `engines: {node: '>=22'}`, which ADMITS 22.0.0-22.12.x -- a range ESLint 10 rejects. That is a real gap this slice must close, not a theoretical one. CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (register-time re-measurement, `pnpm why brace-expansion`): osv-scanner currently reports TWO brace-expansion findings, not one -- 1.1.16 (via minimatch@3.1.5, the eslint 9 chain this slice removes) AND 5.0.7 (via minimatch@10.2.5, pulled in by typescript-eslint@8.62.1's OWN typescript-estree dependency, wholly independent of eslint's version). The original `_acceptance` E10-4 below said this slice would leave osv-scanner reporting zero brace-expansion findings -- that was never achievable from this slice's scope and is corrected in E10-4 and negative_scope. Both are fixed only in 5.0.8; the 5.0.7 instance is a separate, out-of-scope dependency-floor gap recorded as a new backlog follow-up.
_scope_in: Upgrade eslint from ^9.18.0 to ^10 (and @eslint/js in lockstep -- it is versioned with eslint and is 10.0.0+ for the v10 line), regenerate the lockfile, tighten package.json `engines.node` to a range ESLint 10 actually supports, and prove `pnpm lint` still lints the SAME FILE SET with zero errors. Adjust eslint.config.mjs only if v10 requires it -- the config is already flat, so no eslintrc migration is expected.
_design_probe: Required. Before any edit, write .autopilot/state/eslint-10-migration/design-probe.md AND the companion machine-readable baseline .autopilot/state/eslint-10-migration/design-probe-file-list.txt (sorted, repo-relative linted file paths -- verification.focused command 1 diffs against this exact file, so it must exist before the first edit and must not be regenerated after), then STOP for founder confirmation. Pin FOUR things by measurement, not by copying `_design_probe_findings` above: (1) re-run the three compat checks (a)(b)(c) against the tree as it stands at execution time -- `deps-security-bump` may have landed first and moved @next/eslint-plugin-next off 15.5.20, so the plugin grep must be redone on the version actually installed. (2) the exact eslint 10.x version to be installed, with its publish date checked against minimumReleaseAge 10080 (7 days) -- read `npm view eslint time --json` at the VERSION key, never `time.created`. (3) the CURRENT linted-file baseline, written to design-probe-file-list.txt via `npx eslint . -f json` reduced to sorted repo-relative filePath values (same reduction verification.focused command 1 performs). The 2026-07-29 baseline was 81 files (apps 46, packages 31, scripts 3, eslint.config.mjs 1); re-derive it, do not trust that count. (4) whether v10's new config-lookup algorithm changes that set. v10 locates eslint.config.* starting from each linted file's directory instead of cwd; this repo is a pnpm workspace with apps/* and packages/*, and a silently NARROWER file set would make `pnpm lint` pass while checking less -- a green gate that stopped gating. This is the single most likely way this slice ships a regression that looks like success.

_evidence_rules: Re-measure at execution time; the findings recorded in `_design_probe_findings` are dated 2026-07-29/2026-07-31 and are context, not a licence to skip the probe. Read peerDependencies from the INSTALLED package.json under node_modules/.pnpm, not from documentation or memory. Grep the plugin source for removed APIs rather than trusting the absence of a peer range. For publish dates use `npm view <pkg> time --json` and read the exact version key -- `time.created` is the package's first-ever publish and is the wrong field. If any measurement disagrees with what is written above, the measurement wins and the disagreement is recorded.
_timing_gate: Hard external deadline: ESLint v9.x EOL 2026-08-06. Also subject to minimumReleaseAge 10080 (7 days), so the chosen eslint 10.x patch must have been published at least 7 days before the run -- v10.8.0 shipped 2026-07-24 and is eligible from 2026-07-31. Pick the newest ELIGIBLE version, not the newest version; re-check eligibility at execution time since a newer 10.x may have shipped since this was written.
